title: What Do People Actually Want From AI? Mapping Preference Plurality

bias_targets.methodology: Analyzing 1,500 open-ended responses from the PRISM dataset across 75 countries and 8 cultural regions to identify how AI value preferences vary globally using qualitative coding and OLS regression.
Evaluating differences in AI value preferences (e.g., Politeness, Creativity) between male and female/other respondents using regression analysis.
Examining how educational attainment (e.g., graduate/professional degrees) and employment status correlate with requests for specific AI traits like 'Truthfulness' or 'Helpfulness'.
Using age cohorts as predictors in regression models to determine if older or younger users prioritize different AI characteristics.
Testing English proficiency as a predictor variable in regressions to identify if non-native speakers have distinct preferences for AI behavior.
Qualitative thematic analysis of user requests concerning 'neutrality', 'impartiality', and 'AI guardrails' versus 'censorship' or 'political correctness'.
